summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and chronic respiratory conditions was admitted for dysphagia, chills, and increased productive cough with green sputum. Evaluation revealed no signs of bacterial tracheitis on physical exam, chest X-ray, or ENT endoscopy. Labs showed no leukocytosis, and the patient remained afebrile. She was treated symptomatically for a viral upper respiratory infection without antibiotics. Her chronic pain was managed with home medications. Admission labs revealed acute on chronic microcytic anemia with hemoglobin of 6.1 g/dL, prompting a single unit of packed red blood cells; hemoglobin improved to 8.7 g/dL. She was discharged home the following day in stable condition with plans for outpatient follow-up for anemia and ENT evaluation.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period
